concerns.quote: The first reception nurse who saw Mr Williams when he entered HMP Pentonville gave evidence that he had no thoughts of self harm or suicide, but she recorded that he had. It appears she may benefit from additional training and/or supervision. . There was no second reception screen conducted. If Mr Williams was not brought to healthcare staff for his second reception screen then healthcare staff needed to follow this up. . The first reception nurse did not make the referral to the mental health team
concerns.hazard: lack of proper reception screening and mental health referral

concerns.quote: Mr Williams said to several members of staff that he would self harm or hang himself if he wanted something done and it was not happening quickly enough (rather than because he actually wanted to die.) This was recorded on his assessment, care in custody, teamwork (ACCT) document. Some prison officers did not seem familiar with the very important contents of the ACCT, not even the inside cover. concerns.hazard: inadequate understanding of ACCT protocol and risk documentation

She had been given a small card describing code blue and code red (a card which another officer kept about her person and even produced from the witness box), and she still retained that card. concerns.hazard: lack of knowledge about emergency response codes

concerns.quote: The prison officers did not have even the most basic first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training. | am aware from other inquests that this is not provided at a national level. | have written about this before. It seems a significant gap, even allowing for the fact that there are always two trained nurses on site.

concerns.quote: The use of Custodial Nurse [name redacted] (CNPs) in Police custody instead of doctors. The 2003 Home Office circular appeared to envisage nurses working alongside doctors, when this is not how they are deployed. CNPs are also seeing high risk and complex patients without adequate training in mental health. The deployment in Police custody of CNPs places detained persons at risk of death in the future. The 2003 Home Office circular also does not recognise the risk of suicide and self-harm as being
concerns.hazard: use of Custodial Nurse Practitioners in police custody without doctors

concerns.quote: The training of agency staff in the ACCT process and recognising the appropriate threshold to open an ACCT. The training of agency staff in ACCT does not appear to be part of the commissioning process by NHS England and individual providers do not appear to provide training to agency staff in the ACCT process. This places residents in prison at risk of death, given the high level of usage of agency healthcare staff in prison.
concerns.hazard: lack of ACCT process training for agency staff
